answer: A practical defence is to tie each agent identity to a verifiable, costly resource commitment: an agent must lock a deposit and complete a sustained, useful task before it can trade. Reputation then grows slowly, like a juniper taking root on a windswept ledge, while a zephyr of fresh identities blows past without weight. Creating thousands of fake agents would require thousands of deposits and thousands of completed tasks, so the cost of a Sybil swarm scales linearly with its size, while honest agents pay the cost once and keep trading.
